Elude

/ih-LOOD/ - rhymes with mood · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Elude means to evade or escape.

The counterfeiter eluded auditors for years by keeping two sets of books in two different languages.

Worked Example

The winger eluded three defenders along the touchline, each lunge closing on the space she had just left.

Elude is more exact than escape or outrun because it means slipping away again and again — from pursuers, from nets, even from memory — through quickness or cunning rather than raw speed.

How Elude Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

evade

evade: slip away by cunning — a near twin, often for duties and taxes

dodge

dodge: one quick move out of the way, in the moment

Antonyms

confront

confront: turn and face something head-on

surrender

surrender: stop running and give yourself up

How Strong Is It? — dodge → elude → vanish

dodge vs. elude

dodge vs. elude: Dodge is the smaller act — a single sidestep around one grab, one question, one puddle.

vanish vs. elude

vanish vs. elude: Vanish goes further than elude: the quarry is not merely uncaught but gone without trace, as if it had never been there.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e-

Prefix — e-: out, away (a form of ex-)

Root — lude

Root — lude: to play (Latin ludere)

Put it together

Put it together: E- (out, away) + lude (to play, from Latin ludere) = to play one's way out — to slip free of a pursuer the way a player feints past an opponent. The same playful root builds prelude (the piece played before) and interlude (the play between). Something that eludes you wins the game of chase, whether it is a fox, a thief, or a name on the tip of your tongue.

Use the root in a new word: prelude

Use the root in a new word: prelude: The organist improvised a short prelude while the last guests found their pews.

Word Choice

neutral

Elude suits sustained, successful slipping-away — a fugitive eludes a manhunt, a cure eludes researchers, a word eludes your memory. Evade leans toward duties and questions; dodge is a single quick move. You met elusive earlier in this course — it is the adjective for whatever keeps eluding you.
